config.documentTitleFull: WRITTEN REQUEST TO A COUNTY OR MUNICIPAL JAIL OR DETENTION CENTER TO RESTRICT ITS RECORDS FOR AN ALREADY-RESTRICTED OFFENCE, UNDER O.C.G.A. § 35-3-37(k)(2)

primaryStatutoryAuthority.description: An individual who has had criminal history record information restricted may submit a written request to the appropriate county or municipal jail or detention center to have all records for the restricted offence maintained by that jail or detention center restricted. The facility must act within 30 days.
The companion provision on notification of the arresting agency after restriction; its 30-day period is the subject of the recorded open question about when this written request may be sent.

verificationStatute.description: The participant signs the request; no statutory wet-signature rule applies and notarization is not required. The citation is left null and the silence is recorded in sourceSilences.

counselFlags: Georgia does not use "expungement" in the statute and has not since July 1, 2013. The two remedies are record restriction and sealing, and neither destroys the record. The packet must never tell a participant they may state the record does not exist.

A restriction or sealing may still be used to disqualify the participant from employment or office in the same manner as a first offender discharge, and does not supersede disclosure required by federal law.
This is correspondence to a custodial facility, not a court filing. No court, prosecutor or clerk receives notice, there is no proposed order and there is no certificate of service.

Prior restriction of the offence is the statutory precondition of the request. It is a required-before-submission item the participant proves by enclosure, not a condition of generating the letter, and the packet says so.
The facility must restrict access within 30 days of the request, so the packet tells the participant to follow up at day 31 and to send the request by a method that records the date.
The request reaches county and municipal jail and detention center records only. It does not reach private mugshot publishers or background-check vendors that already hold the data.

Whether any Georgia county or municipal jail or detention center publishes its own required form or intake route for this request — which would govern over this generated letter — is an unresolved release-blocking question. Recorded as a blocked component.

Offer this route as a standard follow-on step after the restriction and sealing routes: restriction at the Georgia Crime Information Center and sealing at the clerk do not automatically reach the jail's own records.
The source records the fee for this written request as "None identified." No figure is quoted anywhere in this packet and the fee field is left null.
The source records no fee-waiver route because no fee is identified; the fee-waiver field is left null.

The source records "The participant signs the request. No statutory wet-signature rule applies" and notarization: none, so verificationStatute.citation is left null and the letter carries an ordinary signature block.

Whether the written request may be sent as soon as the record is restricted, or only after the 30-day period for the record centre to notify the arresting agency has run, is an unresolved release-blocking question: the text imposes no waiting period while county prosecutor guidance describes sending the request 30 days after restriction. No waiting period is asserted in the letter and the field is left null.

Self-help stop conditions: The facility refuses the request or does not respond within 30 days. The offence has not in fact been restricted under § 35-3-37, in which case a restriction route comes first. The records the participant is concerned about are held by a private mugshot publisher or background-check vendor, which this route does not reach.

correspondence.subjectLine: Written request under O.C.G.A. § 35-3-37(k)(2) to restrict facility records for an offence whose criminal history record information has already been restricted
bodyParagraphs: My name is {senderName}. I am writing to ask your facility to restrict the records it maintains for an offence for which my criminal history record information has already been restricted under O.C.G.A. § 35-3-37.

The offence is: {offenseRestricted}. I was arrested and booked at your facility in {facilityCounty} on {arrestDate}. My booking number was {bookingNumber}. The court case number for the offence was {caseNumber}.

As far as I know, the record was restricted {restrictionRoute}, on or about {restrictionDate}. I enclose my own proof of that restriction, described below. I am not asking your facility to decide whether the restriction was correct. I am asking it to act on a restriction that has already happened.

O.C.G.A. § 35-3-37(k)(2) provides that an individual who has had criminal history record information restricted may submit a written request to the appropriate county or municipal jail or detention center to have all records for the restricted offence maintained by that jail or detention center restricted, and that the facility restrict access to all such criminal history record information within 30 days of the request. Record restriction by the Georgia Crime Information Center and sealing at the clerk of court do not reach your facility's own records, which is why I am writing to you directly.

I therefore request that your facility restrict access to all records it maintains for the offence identified above. Please send your written response to my mailing address shown at the top of this letter. Thank you for your attention to this request.
enclosures: [COPY OF THE SENDER'S OWN PROOF THAT THE OFFENCE IS ALREADY RESTRICTED — THE CRIMINAL HISTORY REPORT SHOWING THE CYCLE AS RESTRICTED, OR THE RESTRICTING ORDER; SENDER ENCLOSES A COPY ONLY]

provenance.registryExcerpt: An individual who has had criminal history record information restricted pursuant to § 35-3-37 may submit a written request to the appropriate county or municipal jail or detention center to have all records for the restricted offence maintained by that jail or detention center restricted. The facility must act within 30 days. Restriction at GCIC and sealing at the clerk do not reach the jail's own records, so this is a distinct submission to a distinct recipient. Venue: Statewide statute with facility-specific execution. The appropriate county or municipal jail or detention center that holds the booking records for the restricted offence. Destination: The county or municipal jail or detention center that holds the booking records — The written request goes directly to the facility. The facility must restrict access to all such criminal history record information within 30 days of the request. No court is involved. Filing: Send the written request directly to the county or municipal jail or detention center that holds the booking records, citing § 35-3-37(k)(2), with proof that the offence is already restricted enclosed. Follow up at day 31. Fees: None identified. Fee waiver: none — no fee is identified Notice: None. The request goes to the facility; no court, prosecutor or clerk receives notice. Service: No statutory service method. Certified mail is recommended so the participant has a record of the date, because the facility's 30-day compliance period runs from the request. Participant signature: The participant signs the request. No statutory wet-signature rule applies. Notarization: none Consumer-facing copy must say "restrict" and, separately, "seal." Georgia does not use "expungement" in the statute and has not since July 1, 2013, and neither remedy destroys the record. The packet must state that a restriction or sealing may still be used to disqualify the participant from employment or office in the same manner as a first offender discharge under § 42-8-63.1, and does not supersede disclosure required by federal law. The packet must never tell a participant they may state the record does not exist. The packet must tell the participant to follow up at day 31, because the facility must restrict within 30 days of the request. Offer this route as a standard follow-on step after the restriction and sealing routes. Restriction at GCIC and sealing at the clerk do not automatically reach the jail's own records. The participant obtains and encloses proof that the offence is already restricted — the criminal history report showing the cycle as restricted, or the restricting order. Prior restriction is the statutory precondition of the request and is a required-before-submission item, not a condition of generating the request. Exclusion: An offence whose criminal history record information has not been restricted under § 35-3-37. Prior restriction is the statutory precondition. Exclusion: Records held by an entity that is not a county or municipal jail or detention center, including private background-check vendors and mugshot publishers. Waiting period — The criminal history record information has been restricted under § 35-3-37: none stated in § 35-3-37(k)(2) — see the unresolved question on whether the request may be sent immediately or only after the § 35-3-37(k)(1) 30-day agency notification period has run Waiting period — The facility's compliance period after the request: 30 days Unresolved (waiting_period, release_blocker): Whether the § 35-3-37(k)(2) written request may be sent as soon as the criminal history record information is restricted, or only after the 30-day period in § 35-3-37(k)(1) for the center to notify the arresting agency has run. The text of (k)(2) imposes no waiting period; county prosecutor guidance describes sending the request 30 days after the record has been restricted.
